newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea calls for U.N. meeting in submarine drama.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea calls for U.N. meeting in submarine drama.

text.p: North Korea has called a meeting with the United Nations Command on Wednesday and its submarine intrusion into South Korea last month is likely to be on the agenda, a spokesman for the U.N. body said.
The U.S.-led United Nations Command monitors a ceasefire agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Spokesman Jim Coles said on Tuesday that Pyongyang had not specifically said it wanted to discuss the submarine incident during the meeting at the border village of Panmunjom.
"But it's not unreasonable to expect that they'll raise the issue. Our position is that we're going to go to listen to what they have to say," Coles said.

The submarine landed an estimated 26 North Koreans on an east coast beach on September 18. So far, 22 intruders have been shot dead and one captured alive. Five South Korean troops have been killed during a massive manhunt.
Seoul maintains the incident was a commando-style infiltration in preparation for wider military action and breached the terms of the armistice.

Pyongyang says the vessel was on a training mission and drifted into Southern waters after developing engine trouble. It has demanded the immediate return of the submarine and its surviving and dead crew.
North Korean military representatives on the heavily fortified border have twice rejected protest letters from the U.N. Command over the incident.
"The North Koreans have already demanded that the bodies and the submarine be returned, so we can presume that they may want to discuss the issue," Coles said.
The meeting was requested on Monday by the Korean People's Army. "There is nothing special about it, we have meetings like this all the time," Coles added.
Meanwhile, South Korean President Kim Young-sam said the incursion should be punished.

In a speech to mark Armed Forces Day, Kim called the infiltration "an anti-national provocation to the peaceful unification of the fatherland that should be punished in the name of the peace-loving people of the world", the domestic Yonhap news agency reported.
"The North's policy of communising the South has undergone no change whatsoever since the division of the Korean peninsula," Kim said.
"Our armed forces must be fostered into crack units of strength capable of smashing any adventurism of the North, based on a firm superiority in power," Kim added.
